Pule Mabe and his Redisa kariki's

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
Hard hitting on camera confrontation with Mabe and Devi

Summary:
In our story on Redisa, last week, we detailed how Redisa’s directors had failed to create their promised tyre recycling plan and instead over five years they had funneled millions to themselves. But to do that Hermann Erdmann needed friends in high places.

Hermann Erdmann had always claimed he had solid political connections. And In a recent forensic report two of those connections are mentioned. Enoch Godongwana, head of the ANC transformation committee who was paid R100 000 per month by Redisa since 2014, and Pule Mabe –former ANC MP, and former youth league treasurer.


Further information:
MABE
What I find disgusting has been an insistence on perpetuated lies that sought to suggest that we might have done something wrong.

As the extent of Redisa’s misappropriation of funds is uncovered, forensic investigators suggest that our tyre tax paid for a vacation of Mabe’s while he was an MP

Devi
According to the same liquidators they have documents that they say show that Redisa KT paid for your vacation after you left Redisa and even paid for damages to a property and for your catering expenses in excess of R52 000. What happened there?
Mabe
I have never at any given point or time requested KT or Redisa to take up payments of any expenses that had to do with vacations
Devi
So did they or did they not pay for accommodation and damages
Mabe
Well I wouldn’t know because it wasn’t brought to my attention
Devi
Well now you would know because when you stay somewhere, you stay and you pay the bill, that is how you would know
Mabe
Ok, when you are here, you use a car, you stop at a garage you have run out of petrol, you meet me you don’t have cash in your purse, you ask me to put petrol. I use my company credit card, without telling you I am using my company credit card, how are you going to know
Devi
No no see, if you are going on a holiday you pay for the holiday because it’s a holiday
Mabe
So I have never been on a holiday that was funded in that way

But it wasn’t just a holiday. Companies in which Mabe was a director and appears to still have an interest appear to have received R30 million. Carte Blanche confronts Pule Mabe in a hard hitting interview

Script:


Pule Mabe Final Script

Commentary One
Meet Pule Mabe, former treasurer of the ANC youth league, entrepreneur and former member of parliament. Mabe has agreed to speak to us because he feels he has been wrongly accused in a forensic report that suggests he benefitted inappropriately from our tyre tax

PULE MABE
What I find disgusting has been an insistence on perpetuated lies that sought to suggest that we might have done something wrong.

Commentary Two
Last week we reported back on a high court judgement that liquidated Redisa, the tyre recycling plan gazetted in 2012. Since then Redisa has raked in R2.2 billion rand from you the motorist.

Up sound judge Henney
This court has prepared a comprehensive judgement

The judge frowned upon the directors who used Redisa as a get rich quick scheme.
Since 2016, the department of environmental affairs has been investigating REDISA and it was Minister Edna Molewa, once a supporter of this plan who finally asked the courts to liquidate it

Judge Henney
I order that the respondent is placed in final liquidation

Commentary Three
Every time you buy four passenger tyres you pay around R92 in this unseen tax which the manufacturers paid directly to Redisa. Four average truck tyres – you paid Redisa around R616. It was big money and the directors have, despite their repeated denials, misappropriated millions of rands

The Department of environment’s Vanessa Bendeman

Vanessa
We have lodged a complaint with the Hawks. The matter is being investigated
Devi
But will you go after that money
Vanessa
We will, it’s a huge amount of money Devi. Its public funds

Commentary Four
Some of these public funds appear to have landed in the pockets of high ranking ANC figures, like Enoch Godongwana, ANC head of economic transformation. Godongwana has declined to comment for now

Pule Mabe on the other hand has decided to respond.

Pule
There is a clear agenda that those of us who are in leadership structures of the ANC must be seen to be irresponsible and corrupt

Commentary five
Mabe knew CEO of Redisa, Hermann Erdmann before the plan was implemented and was given a well- paid job in the for-profit management company. A year later Mabe left and became a member of parliament, and it’s during this time that the forensic investigators allege your tyre tax paid for his vacation. The reports have been submitted to court

Devi
They have documents that they say show that Redisa KT paid for your vacation after you left Redisa and even paid for damages to a property and for your catering expenses, in excess of R52 000. What happened there?
Mabe
I have never at any given point or time requested KT or Redisa to take up payments of any expenses that had to do with vacations
Devi
So, did they or did they not pay for accommodation and damages
Mabe
Well I wouldn’t know because it wasn’t brought to my attention
Devi
Well now you would know because when you stay somewhere, you stay and you pay the bill, that is how you would know
Mabe
Ok, when you are here, you use a car, you stop at a garage you have run out of petrol, you meet me you don’t have cash in your purse, you ask me to put petrol. I use my company credit card, without telling you I am using my company credit card, how are you going to know
Devi
No no see, if you are going on a holiday you pay for the holiday because it’s a holiday
Mabe
So, I have never been on a holiday that was funded in that way

Commentary six
But Mabe later reiterated to our producer that it wasn’t a holiday

Mabe
I was not on a holiday

Commentary seven
Instead it seems your tyre tax paid for Mabe to attend an ANC birthday bash in Cape Town


Mabe
Exactly in that same year that people are making reference to a vacation, there was going to Jan 08th of the ANC in CT

Commentary eight
Pule Mabe resigned as an MP recently when his place was taken by Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma

Devi
Ordinary South Africans are watching this
Mabe
I am not a member of parliament so these questions that you are asking me
Devi
Then you were a member of parliament
Mabe
It doesn’t matter I am not a member of parliament now
Devi
It does matter
Mabe
It can matter to you I am not going to answer that question. I am not a member of parliament now.

Commentary nine
The more serious claim by the forensic investigators is that Mabe’s companies invoiced and were paid R30 million rand of our tyre tax in questionable payments when he was an MP.

They say his 2016 parliamentary declaration shows he was a director of Kariki media and Enviromobi, the companies that benefitted. Mabe disputes this

Devi
The point they make is that 2015 it shows there was no interest and then in 2016 the declaration shows you were a director back at Kariki media
Mabe
It’s a lie its illegal, all smacks of negativity that seeks to project me in a negative light

Commentary ten
The payments are invoiced for a series of TV programmes and a roll out of these vehicles. These 40 Tuk Tuks cost us R5 million rand, each one R125 000. About 3x more than the cost of a Tuc Tuc.

Up sound this is TUK TUK
This is the tuk tuk that Alan Greyling…. And that is your kariki

Mabe insists these are not TUC TUCS and cannot be priced the same



MABE
This is a tuc- tuc. A tuc tuc carries people from Sandton to Rosebank. A kariki has a loader and a hydraulic thing, all sorts of things, and a seat belt.

Commentary eleven
Mabe is fuming because the forensic investigators questioned the existence of the karikis’ But they were all here in this warehouse. What is odd is that Redisa bought the kariki’s from the company in which Mabe has an interest, and then donated them back to the very same company.

Mabe
The cars that Redisa brought in were a donation to a programme
Devi
Redisa donated what?
Mabe
The cars the forty tuk tuks
Devi
They karikis they are not tuk tuks
Mabe
Ya because people have lied in the document
Devi
No now you don’t believe that now you keep telling me – you use the right words now
That is a kariki – Redisa donated that
Yes
Devi
Why is it parked here and not doing work?
Mabe
Because, because, because an allegation was made against us that these cars don’t exist.

Commentary 12
This week the forensic investigator told Carte Blanche they stand by their report, and the investigation is ongoing. Mabe meanwhile is rolling out his Kariki’s across municipalities to assist with waste collection

THE END 7 04

PROMO ONE
Last week we reported back on a high court judgement that liquidated the tyre recycling plan Redisa. This week Pule Mabe responds to allegations against him


PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Former MP Pule Mabe responds to a forensic report

Mabe
I am not a member of parliament so these questions that you are asking me
Devi
Then you were a member of parliament
Mabe
It doesn’t matter I am not a member of parliament now
Devi
It does matter


PROMO THREE 15 seconds
Did former MP Pule Mabe accept questionable payments from your tyre tax?

Devi
So, did they or did they not pay for accommodation and damages
Mabe
Well I wouldn’t know because it wasn’t brought to my attention
Devi
Well now you would know because when you stay somewhere, you stay and you pay the bill, that is how you would know
Pule
Ok
